decision_reason: An indexed explicit adjacency representation is easier to inspect edge by edge, but its serialized map is much larger for the representative 100x100 task.

v13_8x8_reconstruction.note: The baseline user/system messages and byte counts were reconstructed from the archived v13 task. Candidate bytes are serialization size, not provider token usage or price.

traditional_seed0_100x100_size_audit.endpoint_basis: Stored true pickup/dropoff IDs were used as surrogate already-resolved endpoint IDs for package and serialization sizing only. The offline candidate message represented them as ordinary route_query endpoints; it was not sent or treated as a model result, and no true_* field name was added.
traditional_seed0_100x100_size_audit.note: This is an offline size audit on one representative task, not a model call or a route-quality result. The 100x100 compact-map number covers the map payload; the candidate full-user-message number includes the query and contract.

conclusions: Qwen and DeepSeek do not need byte-identical prompts because they perform different stages.
The canonical map, directed-edge facts, costs, endpoint IDs, map version, and validation rules must remain consistent across stage-specific views.
The candidate explicit adjacency representation was not adopted as the default because of its large input growth at 100x100 scale.
The active R4 builder remains on directional-cost-grid-v1; its regenerated v13 messages match the archived system and user message hashes exactly.
No API-token estimate, price estimate, route success claim, or formal-experiment result is produced by this audit.
